referents.why: Second person masculine singular in direct address; the psalm shifts from third-person LORD in 23:1-3 to address here, so the addressee is the LORD, the same masculine singular named in verse 1.
referents.category: second person address to God within a psalm

referents.why: First person common singular object in the psalm's own speech; no other speaker is quoted here.
Second person masculine singular possessive on rod; the rod belongs to the addressee of the speech, the LORD.
referents.category: possessive second person in address to God

referents.why: Second person masculine singular possessive on staff; same addressee as the rod, the LORD.
referents.category: possessive second person in address to God

referents.why: Third person masculine plural subject of a plural act (comfort). No single candidate is plural; the composite of rod and staff is the pair that comforts, and the masculine plural is the default for a mixed pair.
referents.category: plural pronoun for a composite of two objects

referents.why: First person common singular object in the psalm's own speech.
Implied first person common singular subject of the yiqtol verb, in the psalm's own voice.
Implied first person common singular subject of the negated yiqtol, in the psalm's own voice.

links.why: The clause opens with ki (for, because) after its main clause; the reason is cl2, and the edge runs from the explained clause to its reason, as the builder has it.
links.category: reason clause after its main clause

links.why: The builder type conceded is not in link_types. The relation is the explicit concession gam ki, which the list names as the though type, so this link is replaced by the add below.
Gam ki (even though) opens cl0 and qualifies the claim of cl1: I will not fear, even though I walk through the valley. It is explicit, not the verse-initial ki case, and it attaches forward to cl1.

groups.why: The obstacle is cl0, the claim that holds anyway is cl1, and its ground is cl2, the ki clause. The group kind names exactly these three roles.

none_fit.what: cl3 is a verbless noun phrase (your rod and your staff) that is the topic of cl4, and cl4's subject 'they' takes it up. No link type or group kind says that a nominal clause supplies the subject of the following clause (a left-dislocated topic).

cant_tell.what: How cl3 and cl4 attach to the reason. They follow cl2 with no conjunction, after a semicolon. The text may give a second ground under the same ki (the rod and staff as a further reason for not fearing), or a separate asyncetic line. The form does not decide, so no link or group is added for them here.
cant_tell.why: There is no conjunction at cl3. A because link from cl4 to cl1 would assert a reading that the form does not settle.
